{"id": "64c23ede-f68f-451a-92ea-21c7b3b2589b", "role": "assistant", "block_type": "tool_summary", "content": [{"type": "tool_result", "tool_use_id": "tooluse_I8fStpg8HAXQYlHsAAj5ok", "status": "success", "content": [{"text": "{\"content\":{\"result\":[{\"rank_order\":1,\"title\":\"Remediating exposures for Amazon S3 buckets\",\"context\":\"# Remediating exposures for Amazon S3 buckets\\n\\nAWS Security Hub can generate exposure findings for Amazon Simple Storage Service (Amazon S3) buckets.\\n\\nOn the Security Hub console, the Amazon S3 bucket involved in an exposure finding and its identifying information are listed in\\nthe **Resources** section of the finding details. Programmatically, you can retrieve resource\\ndetails with the GetFindingsV2 operation of the Security Hub CSPM API.\\n\\nAfter identifying the resource involved in an exposure finding, you can delete the resource if you don't need it.\\nDeleting a nonessential resource can reduce your exposure profile and AWS costs. If the resource is essential,\\nfollow these recommended remediation steps to help mitigate the risk. The remediation topics are\\ndivided based on the type of trait.\\n\\nA single exposure finding contains issues identified in multiple remediation topics. Conversely, you can address an exposure finding and bring down\\nits severity level by addressing just one remediation topic. Your approach to risk remediation\\ndepends on your organizational requirements and workloads.\\n\\n**Note:**\\n\\nThe remediation guidance provided in this topic might require additional consultation in other AWS resources.\\n\\n###### Contents\\n\\n* Misconfiguration traits for Amazon S3 buckets\\n\\n + The Amazon S3 bucket has versioning disabled\\n + The Amazon S3 bucket has Object Lock disabled\\n + Amazon S3 bucket is not encrypted at rest with AWS KMS keys\\n + Multi-factor authentication (MFA) delete is disabled on a versioned Amazon S3 bucket\\n + The Amazon S3 bucket allows principals from other AWS accounts to modify bucket permissions\\n* Reachability traits for Amazon S3 buckets\\n\\n + The Amazon S3 bucket has public read access\\n + The Amazon S3 bucket has public write access\\n* Sensitive data traits for Amazon S3 buckets\\n\\n + The Amazon S3 bucket contains sensitive data\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/securityhub/latest/userguide/exposure-s3-bucket.html\"},{\"rank_order\":2,\"title\":\"Identify public Amazon S3 buckets in AWS Organizations by using Security Hub CSPM\",\"context\":\"## Additional information\\n\\n*Workflow for monitoring public Amazon S3 buckets*\\n\\nThe following workflow illustrates how you can monitor the public Amazon S3 buckets in your organization. The workflow assumes that you completed the steps in the *Configure the Amazon SNS topic and email subscription* story of this pattern*.*\\n\\n1. You receive an email notification when an Amazon S3 bucket is configured with public access.\\n\\n * If the bucket is approved for public access, set the workflow status of the corresponding finding to `SUPPRESSED` in the Security Hub CSPM administrator account. This prevents Security Hub CSPM from issuing further notifications for this bucket and helps reduce duplicate alerts.\\n * If the bucket isn't approved for public access, set the workflow status of the corresponding finding in the Security Hub CSPM administrator account to `NOTIFIED`. This prevents Security Hub CSPM from issuing further notifications for this bucket and helps reduce unnecessary alerts.\\n2. If the bucket might contain sensitive data, turn off public access immediately until the review is completed. If you turn off public access, then Security Hub CSPM changes the workflow status to `RESOLVED`. Then, email notifications for the bucket stop.\\n3. Find the user who configured the bucket as public (for example, by using AWS CloudTrail) and start a review. The review results in either removing public access to the bucket or approving public access. If public access is approved, then set the workflow status of the corresponding finding to `SUPPRESSED`.\\n\\n*Security considerations*\\n\\n* Grant only the minimum IAM permissions described in the *Prerequisites* section. Don't use service-wide wildcard actions (such as `securityhub:*`) or wildcard resources.\\n* This pattern doesn't require you to disable Security Hub CSPM, AWS Config, or any logging controls. Keep these services enabled in all accounts and Regions to help maintain continuous detection of public Amazon S3 buckets.\\n* Suppress a finding only after the bucket owner and security team have documented approval for public access, and review suppressed findings periodically.\\n* Restrict the Amazon SNS topic policy so that only the Amazon EventBridge rule in your account can publish to it (for example, by using an `aws:SourceArn` condition), and encrypt the topic with AWS KMS\",\"url\":\"https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/patterns/identify-public-s3-buckets-in-aws-organizations-using-security-hub.html\"},{\"rank_order\":3,\"title\":\"securing-s3-buckets\",\"skill_description\":\"Create and secure S3 buckets following AWS best practices for access control, encryption, monitoring, and remediation of misconfigurations. Use when the user wants to secure a new bucket, audit an existing bucket, fix a security finding, configure encryption, or enable logging and monitoring. Do NOT use for general S3 data operations, S3 Tables setup, or discovering existing data assets.\\n\\n\\nServices: s3, kms, cloudtrail, guardduty, config, accessanalyzer\\nTasks: secure, audit, remediate, encrypt, monitor\\nPersona: developer, security-engineer\\nWorkload: storage, compliance\\n*\",\"skill_name\":\"securing-s3-buckets\"}]}}"}]}], "label": "Look up Security Hub S3 public read remediation guidance"}

{"id": "2fec08fa-5068-4177-ad66-1d7add239a74", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "For a single flagged bucket, I'd use **`AWSConfigRemediation-ConfigureS3BucketPublicAccessBlock`**. It's a good fit for Security Hub S3 public access findings.

**Why this one**
- It applies S3 Block Public Access to that one bucket, using the `BucketName` parameter.
- `BlockPublicAcls`, `BlockPublicPolicy`, `IgnorePublicAcls` and `RestrictPublicBuckets` all default to `true`, so the defaults block all public access.
- `AutomationAssumeRole` is required. The role needs `s3:GetBucketPublicAccessBlock` and `s3:PutBucketPublicAccessBlock`. It also needs `s3:GetAccountPublicAccessBlock` and `s3:PutAccountPublicAccessBlock`, and the `ssm:StartAutomationExecution` and `ssm:GetAutomationExecution` actions.
- Run it in **us-west-2**, or in the Region where the bucket's Automation runs. The bucket name is the only value you need to supply.

**Alternatives**

| Runbook | Scope | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `AWS-DisableS3BucketPublicReadWrite` | Single bucket | It disables public read and write through Block Public Access. The role is optional, because it falls back to the caller's permissions. It's a simpler option, but you have less control over the individual settings. |
| `AWSSupportRemediator-BlockS3BucketPublicAccess` | Single bucket | It's built for Security Hub CSPM findings such as "block public read access". It's idempotent, so it makes no changes if the bucket is already blocked. It requires Business Support+, Enterprise Support, or Unified Operations Support. |
| `AWSConfigRemediation-ConfigureS3PublicAccessBlock` | **Whole account** | It sets account-level Block Public Access. Use it only if you want to lock down every bucket in the account. |

**Before you run it**
- Confirm the bucket isn't meant to be public, for example for static website hosting or a CloudFront origin. Blocking public access can break those setups.
- If a CloudFormation stack manages the bucket, the change can cause stack drift. Update the template too.
- Block Public Access doesn't remove the public ACL or bucket policy. It overrides them. Clean those up afterward so the configuration doesn't depend on the block staying in place.
- Check CloudTrail to see who or what made the bucket public.

I can check the bucket's current Block Public Access settings, ACL and policy in us-west-2 if you give me the bucket name and account ID. I can also run the runbook. Any change would need your approval first.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
